subject: ACME MAP: Technical Evaluation Plan (benchmark criteria + shortlist)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME MAP: Technical Evaluation Plan (benchmark criteria + shortlist)

Hi Emily / Raj 

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap + next steps to keep the MAP moving:

Call recap (30m):
- Discussed ACME's GenAI search use case (embedded product summaries + retrieval-augmented generation).
- Key constraints: P95 latency target for inference, cost per 1k tokens, and strict data residency for some datasets.
- ACME will run a technical eval to validate candidate models and config.

Attached: draft MAP workbook (ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx) and our internal benchmark guide (redwood-benchmark-guide.pdf).

Proposed MAP milestone: Technical evaluation plan (owner: Redwood + ACME eng)
- Goal: Produce benchmark report showing (1) quality vs baseline, (2) latency at target concurrency, (3) cost per 1k tokens / per-query, and (4) operational notes (KV cache hit rates, memory footprint).
- Success criteria (ACME suggested / Redwood proposal):
  - Quality: >= 5% improvement in top-1 relevance over current baseline on ACME dev set (we'll take your eval prompts).
  - Latency: P95 <= 150 ms for 512-token requests at 8 concurrent connections (measured cold and warm).
  - Throughput: sustain 200 requests/minute with end-to-end 95th latency <200 ms.
  - Cost: target inference cost under $0.08 per 1k tokens (post-quantization/ batching optimizations); we will show cost sensitivity matrix.

Model shortlist (initial):
- Llama 2 70B-chat (quantized 4-bit / int8)
- Mistral 7B Instruct (optimized for latency)
- OpenAssistant-13B (balanced quality/cost)
- Redmond-13B (customer-friendly medium-size variant)

Test plan / infra:
- Redwood will provision a dedicated test pool (GPU-backed) and run the benchmark harness with both hosted and private deployment configurations (if you prefer VPC test we can coordinate).
- ACME to provide: representative prompt set (sanitized), sample document corpus for retrieval (S3 link or Drive), and a point-of-contact for engineering and security.

Proposed timeline / target close:
- Deliver MAP draft: Mar 4 (you should have workspace attached)  ACTION: Emily review + comments
- Benchmark runs scheduled: Mar 1218 (prelim results Mar 19)  OWNER: Redwood (Camila + Dylan)
- Final evaluation & recommendation: Apr 22, 2027  TARGET CLOSE

Next steps (short):
1) Emily: confirm timeline and provide sanitized prompts + sample corpus by Mar 5
2) ACME security: confirm deployment preference (Hosted vs VPC) and list required compliance artifacts
3) Marissa/Camila: finalize benchmark config and schedule runs (we'll share run slots)

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook, milestone owner columns) | redwood-benchmark-guide.pdf (test harness & metrics)

Thanks  happy to hop on a 15m follow-up if helpful.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME MAP: Technical Evaluation Plan (benchmark criteria + shortlist)

Thanks Marissa  this looks like a good starting point. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Test data: we can share a sanitized dev prompts set and a subset of our product corpus (S3). Will need a short DPIA confirmation: will Redwood process any real PII during the benchmark? We prefer to avoid it.
2) VPC: we likely prefer the private (VPC) test run to reflect production networking and latency  is this feasible during the Mar 1218 window?
3) Security milestone: can we add a pre-benchmark "security checklist" item (SOC2 evidence, network allowlist, temporary keys) to the MAP?

We'll try to get the artifacts to you by Mar 5  Raj will own the sample corpus upload. One more ask: can you include which quantization levels you'll test and the expected delta in latency/cost (ballpark)?

Emily Turner
Director, Product Engineering | ACME Corp
emily.turner@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME MAP: Technical Evaluation Plan (benchmark criteria + shortlist)

Emily  thanks, great questions. Details below and I updated the MAP workbook (v1.1).

Security / PII: Redwood will not process real PII for benchmark runs unless you explicitly provide it. If you send sanitized samples we will use those. We'll also provide the SOC 2 summary and a short checklist ahead of any VPC test.

VPC test window: Yes  we can run VPC-based benchmarks in the Mar 1218 window. We will need a short window (12 days) of ACL allowlist and one temporary test key from your infra team.

Quantization / expected deltas (ballpark):
- FP16 -> int8/4-bit (quantized) usually shows 23x throughput improvement and ~2040% latency reduction depending on kernel support and model size.
- We will test both 8-bit and 4-bit quantization profiles where supported (models + accuracy trade-offs documented).

Owners & responsibilities (updated):
- Redwood (Camila): benchmark harness, run orchestration, result deck
- Redwood (Dylan): model provisioning, quantization profiles, infra allocation
- ACME (Raj): upload sanitized corpus to S3 + provide POC for allowlist/key exchange
- ACME (Emily): review & accept success criteria, sign-off on final recommendation

Updated timeline:
- MAP v1.1 sent (attached)  Mar 3 (DONE)
- ACME artifacts due  Mar 5 (ACME)
- Infra & allowlist exchange  Mar 810
- Benchmark runs (VPC + hosted)  Mar 1218 (Camila/Dylan)
- Preliminary results  Mar 19
- Final recommendation  Apr 22

Let us know if you'd like us to include an explicit "pre-benchmark security checklist" milestone (we can add it to the MAP with a discrete owner/date).

Thanks  I'll loop Dylan to provision the models and reserve the test slots.

Marissa
